content: 1. The presence of mucopurulent cervical discharge is indicative of cervicitis. 2. Pregnant or breastfeeding women were excluded from certain studies. 3. Microbiological cure, clinical cure, and adverse events were evaluated in studies using ceftriaxone 250 mg intramuscularly as a single dose. 4. In Japan, a study involving Japanese men with gonococcal urethritis reported a median age of 30 years. Men who did not attend follow-up visits were excluded. 5. A randomized study in China included non-pregnant women aged 18–65 years with uncomplicated urethral or cervical gonorrhea. Participants agreed to abstain from sexual intercourse or use condoms until the study was completed. 6. Exclusion criteria included a history of epilepsy, kidney or liver insufficiency, gastrointestinal, hematologic, or cardiovascular disease, immunodeficiency, allergy to quinolone antibiotics, disseminated gonococcal infection, or recent use of systemic antibiotics. 7. Evidence-to-decision frameworks and systematic reviews were used to update WHO treatment guidelines for Neisseria gonorrhoeae. 8. In the USA, a randomized study included men and non-pregnant women aged 18–55 years with signs and symptoms of urogenital gonorrhea. Participants were required to abstain from sexual intercourse for seven days after treatment and use contraception for 30 days before and after treatment. 9. Complicated gonorrhea cases, such as pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) or epididymitis, were excluded. Patients with recent systemic or intravaginal antibiotic use, known allergies to cephalosporins or penicillin, or HIV infection on antiretroviral therapy were also excluded. 10. In Bhutan, a study included men and women suspected of gonococcal urethritis and prescribed empirical therapy. Clinical cure was assessed, but microbiological outcomes were not reported. 11. In Botswana, a study included pregnant women aged 18 years or older with gestational age less than 35 weeks. Participants were required to return for follow-up care. 12. In China, a study included men with uncomplicated gonococcal urethritis presenting with lower urinary tract symptoms or mucopurulent urethral discharge. Complicated or disseminated gonococcal infections were excluded. 13. In the USA, a study included heterosexual men and women with uncomplicated anogenital gonorrhea. Pregnant or nursing women, patients with allergies to beta-lactam antibiotics, or those who had received antibiotics within the past two weeks were excluded. 14. In the United Kingdom, a study included men and women with uncomplicated anogenital gonorrhea diagnosed by the presence of Gram-negative intracellular diplococci (GNID) in smears. 15. In Canada, a study included men who have sex with men (MSM) with positive cultures for Neisseria gonorrhoeae from any site or GNID from urethral or rectal swabs. 16. In Germany, a study included men and women with uncomplicated urethritis and proctitis confirmed by culture. Patients who did not return for follow-up within four weeks were excluded. 17. In the USA, a study included men and women with uncomplicated urogenital gonorrhea. Pregnant or breastfeeding women were excluded. 18. In China, a study included men and women with simple genital gonorrhea. Microbiological and clinical cure rates were assessed. 19. In the USA, a study included women with uncomplicated cervical, urethral, anal, or pharyngeal gonorrhea confirmed by culture or history of exposure to a man with documented gonococcal urethritis. 20. In the USA, a study included men and women with pharyngeal and anorectal gonorrhea confirmed by positive smears or documented exposure. 21. In the USA, a study included men and women with uncomplicated urethral, cervical, or anal gonorrhea. Patients with active liver or kidney disease, myasthenia gravis, bleeding disorders, or recent antimicrobial therapy were excluded.
